data.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar's CLI facade on current main is 714 lines and reconstructs command identity and policy through 19 overlapping frozensets, an intercept ladder, package-help filenames, a regex-based reference generator, and manually repeated test censuses. Adding a command requires synchronized edits across routing, mount/init policy, confirmation/output behavior, help, documentation, and tests. This has regrown the facade after its prior split and creates drift risk at hard-won compatibility seams.

Twenty-one intercept-only commands have no package-data help. `rebar help <command>` reports them unknown, while handler-owned `<command> --help` is inconsistent and can execute real work; `enrich --help` entered the handler in the recovered probe. The maintainer approved normalizing every visible top-level command to canonical package-data help, including a comprehensive grouped overview.

## Approved Architecture
Create one stdlib-only immutable lazy route registry. A canonical route records its spellings and visibility, lazy `module:function` handler plus a bounded invocation-adapter kind, package-data help resource, best-effort mount policy, strict initialization policy or narrow selector, confirmation/output policy, and possible semantic capabilities. Exact aliases live on their route; compatibility shims are first-class routes with replacement metadata. The registry is a routing table, not another parser, plugin system, dependency-injection container, or middleware framework.

Top-level overview/help, alias help, malformed global syntax, and unknown-command rendering run before RP-04 operation-snapshot composition, config discovery/materialization, store mount, handler resolution, and optional imports. Every visible command supports byte-authoritative `rebar <command> --help`/`-h` and `rebar help <command>`. Nested help remains handler-owned but must be lean and side-effect-free.

A separate semantic capability registry maps a capability to its packaging extra and missing posture: `error`, `unavailable`, `abstain`, or intentional `fallback`. Command routes advertise possible capabilities for introspection only. The selected handler/backend checks a capability after it has parsed enough context to know the capability is required; existing domain components continue to own unavailable/abstain/fallback result shapes.

## Compatibility Contracts
Package-data bytes remain authoritative. Help/unknown paths never mount. Store-touching execution retains central best-effort mount and strict init. Command-specific confirmation, global output extraction, legacy JSON shapes, and tokens after `--` remain unchanged. `audit show` remains lean while `audit serve` alone requires UI; lean review/workflow diagnostic modes remain available; metrics, grounding, and rich-text degradation retain their current postures.

Exact aliases reuse canonical help. `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`, and `jira-onboard` retain alias-specific help naming the canonical replacement, and `jira-onboard` keeps its historical usage spelling. Hidden `bridge-status` resolves explicit help but is absent from overview/discovery. Retired `purge-bridge` remains unknown. `rebar-mcp` remains a separate entry point.

## Migration and Rollback
Use expand/contract. First add and validate the registry while deriving compatibility exports and shadow-checking current policy. Then move help/lookup, core execution, capability boundaries, and registry consumers. Remove legacy frozensets, intercept parsing, curated reference censuses, and compatibility exports only after behavioral and distribution contracts pass. During expansion, rollback switches dispatch back to the derived compatibility exports; after contraction, code revert restores the prior route without any stored-data migration. Ticket, event, bridge, and binding formats do not change.

## Scope
In scope: the `rebar` top-level route/help boundary, command and capability registries, existing handlers' selected-capability checks, canonical help resources, overview/reference generation, lean/full-extra contract tests, migration guards, and an ADR. Out of scope: redesigning nested command parsers, adding a plugin API, changing MCP into a CLI verb, changing domain fallback payloads, or changing RP-04 configuration ownership.

RP-04's remaining contract/cutover work owns overlapping composition seams. This epic depends on `vibrant-legal-hind`; the exact overlap is `junior-lepidolite-boa`.

## Delivery Order
1. Record the architecture decision.
2. Establish validated registry-backed canonical help and pre-operation routing.
3. In parallel after that contract, migrate core execution and semantic capability boundaries.
4. Derive docs/distribution checks from the registry.
5. Retire compatibility censuses and complete cutover.

## Testing
Use in-process unit tests for pure registry validation. Use real CLI subprocess contract tests for exact bytes, streams, exit codes, alias/retirement behavior, and absence of config/mount/handler effects. Use a clean no-extras wheel for every top-level help form and heavy-import exclusion. Use a full-extra lane to resolve every lazy handler/selector and exercise selected capability postures. Existing CLI, mount, output, bridge, audit, LLM, metrics, rendering, grounding, and provider tests remain the behavioral oracles; shadow parity is required before dispatch cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every canonical visible command appears exactly once in the grouped overview and returns its committed package-data bytes from both top-level help forms before any operation/config/store/handler boundary.
- [ ] Exact aliases, compatibility shims, hidden aliases, and retired spellings exhibit the approved help/discovery behavior, including historical `jira-onboard` usage and unknown `purge-bridge`.
- [ ] Real command execution routes lazily through one validated registry while preserving mount/init, argv, confirmation, stream, exit-code, and legacy-output contracts.
- [ ] Selected optional modes/backends use semantic capability metadata and preserve each approved `error`/`unavailable`/`abstain`/`fallback` behavior without eager optional imports.
- [ ] CLI reference generation, route/help coverage, lean-wheel checks, and full-extra reference resolution enumerate the registries rather than regex/manual command censuses.
- [ ] Duplicate registries and compatibility exports are removed after shadow parity; the facade and new modules satisfy the repository module-size and complexity gates with no stored-data migration.
- [ ] ADR 0099 and the living architecture document record the route, capability, migration, compatibility, and rollback boundaries.
data.title: RP-05 — Lazy CLI command and capability registry with canonical help
